subject: flamingo
pitch: An elegant flamingo standing tall in shallow water. Candy-pink feathers deepening to coral on the wings, with a flash of black flight feathers at the wing tips, an S-curved neck, a bent beak that is pale pink with a black tip, pale yellow eyes and long rose-coloured legs with knobbly knees and webbed feet.
reasoning:
I'm planning the flamingo's proportions and pose—standing on two separated legs at about 1.3m tall with legs around 0.8m—and considering adding a thin water disc beneath it to suggest it's standing in shallow water.

I'm working out the skeleton structure: a hips root joint feeding into a spine chain shaped by catmull points for the egg-like body, with coordinates for tail, chest, and neck placement, plus a sweep function to loft the body geometry along that spine.

Now I'm extending the body shape rearward past the spine chain, defining a radius function to taper the body from a small tail to a rounder chest using a sine-based easing curve. For color, I'm going with a mottled candy pink for the body with coral accents on the wings.

I'm adding a short tail by creating a separate joint chain running back and down from the hips, then sweeping a tapered, flattened profile along it to form rump feathers.

Now I'm figuring out overall proportions — scaling the flamingo's height to around 1.4m with legs about 0.7-0.8m, setting the hip and body center heights, and planning an S-curve neck path running from the chest up toward where the head will sit.

For the legs, I'm working out the real flamingo anatomy: the visible "knee" is actually the ankle, with the hidden femur tucked close to the body and the tibiotarsus forming the visible upper leg bending backward. I'm placing hip joints and working out limb segment lengths (roughly 0.42 each) so the total reach matches the hip-to-ground distance, with the bend direction set to flex backward like a real flamingo knee.

Now I'm planning the feet: three front toes fanning out from the ankle tip, with the middle toe longer than the side toes, and webbing membranes stretched between adjacent toe chains to capture that distinctive flamingo foot shape.

For the water, I'll make it a flat opaque pale blue disc acting as the floor itself, with the feet sinking slightly into it so nothing floats above the surface.

Adjusting the numbers so the ankle sits at 0.03 with toes just above the water surface, and adding light ripple ring tori around each foot to sell the water contact. Now I'm working on the leg segment radii, tapering the tibia thickness as it sweeps up the chain.

Knee bends backward like a real flamingo's, so I'm working out the leg segment lengths and foot target so the two-bone chain reaches with a slight backward knee bend rather than being perfectly straight, computing the bend height from the segment lengths versus the hip-to-foot distance.

Now I'm placing the hip root near the body's center of mass, keeping the legs close to the midline. For the wings, I'm planning them as a joint chain from shoulder to tail, folded against the body sides, and I'll build the visible feather layers using extruded shapes — coral coverts layered over black pointed flight feathers at the wingtip, modeled in side-view outline.

Still tilting the wing geometry inward toward the back, then I'll layer black spiky flight feather tips over the rear of the coral wing base.

Still shaping the wing feather outline...

I'm checking the wing's position relative to the narrowed rear body, confirming the wing hangs free past the body with a slight inward tilt, which I'll bump up to 0.2. I'm also planning layered coverts in coral tones with scalloped edges, plus small scapulars and a pink base for the wing.

For coloring, I'm setting up a gradient from pink at the front to coral at the back along the body, and a similar gradient for the wing from a lighter pink to coral. I'm also considering adding a couple of extruded scallop layers for texture on the coverts, and starting to think through how to rig the wing joints as a chain with shoulder, elbow, and tip points.

Now I'm figuring out the neck: starting from the chest at the front of the body, I'm plotting an S-curve path of points rising upward with forward and backward bends like a goose-neck, aiming for a total standing height around 1.6 meters consistent with flamingo proportions, with the head sitting near the top of that curve.

I'll taper the radius from 0.075 down to around 0.03 along the sweep, sculpt the tube with that pink material, and attach the neck chain as a child of the chest joint rather than floating independently in the body.

Then I'm positioning the head joint at the top of the neck, aiming it slightly forward and down to give the flamingo a natural bent-beak posture, and sizing a small scaled sphere for the skull. For eyes I'm placing tiny pale yellow spheres with small black pupils symmetrically on each side, using local coordinate offsets while being careful about which direction "left" and "right" actually mean in the model's local frame.

Now I'm shaping the beak as a downward-bending bezier curve, building upper and lower mandible paths from head-local points that bend sharply partway and taper toward the tip.

Still shaping the lower mandible curve points so the tip nests just beneath the upper beak's tip, adjusting the forward/down offsets for each control point.

Now I'm working out how the head joint attaches to the end of the neck chain, making sure the parent reference points to the last neck joint and the head sphere is centered at that position.

Thinking about head orientation given the neck's upward-forward tangent, so the beak should angle forward-down. I'm sizing the head sphere with a slightly elongated scale, adding a small forehead bump, and placing the beak emerging from the front of the head at roughly realistic flamingo proportions—about 0.155 in length with a matching base thickness.

Now I'm scattering small flattened sphere "feathers" across the body surface to add texture, filtering placement to the upper portion and orienting them to flow backward along the body with an elongated scale so they look like scalloped plumage.

Defining the color palette now—pink, coral, black, rose legs, yellow beak tones, and water/ripple hues—keeping the total under 64 colors, then starting the body mottle paint pass before moving to wings.

Setting up the leg chains now, parenting each to the hips with unique joint names per side (hipL/kneeL/ankleL vs hipR/kneeR/ankleR) and contact points. I'm checking whether the limb function returns an array of joint positions that the chain builder can consume directly as a polyline path.

Now I'm placing thigh-covering feather spheres at the hip, scaled and positioned per side, then working out toe tip coordinates branching from the ankle joint — middle, outer, and inner toes with slightly offset x/z positions.

Still building toe chains...

For the webbing, I'll construct a horizontal slab polygon by ordering points around the toes and pulling midpoints back toward the foot for a natural web shape, using a small helper to interpolate between vectors.

I'm adding small spheres for a knobbly knee and ankle joint, keeping them low-poly and flattened where needed, plus a thin cylinder for the water surface rigged to the hips bone since it should stay rigid.

Now I'm placing ripple torus shapes around each foot, rotated flat to lie on the water surface, sized in pairs plus one larger ring. For the tail, I'm keeping it small and tapered in pink using a short chained path with two points rather than a full feathered sweep, since the wingtips mostly cover it anyway.

I'm setting up the hip joint and spine chain as a catmull path from hips upward through two more points, parented under hips with a spine role, while the body itself gets its own sweep path from the tail region through the torso with a widening radius toward the back.

Now I'm checking the anatomy details: thighs sit inside the body outline, the neck base meets the chest smoothly, and I'm tuning the body's ellipse radius function so it peaks correctly. I'm also working out where the wings should attach by calculating the body's half-width at that point along the sweep curve, adjusting the easing formula so the taper peaks at the right parameter value.

Checking the wing position near the front where t is around 0.7, the width works out fine with slight tilt, and the rear body narrows appropriately as t drops toward 0.15.

With tilt applied along the wing's x-direction, I find it needs reducing to 0.05 so the wing floats just off the body surface rather than embedding into it. I'm setting up the joint chain for the wing — shoulder, elbow, and tip positions — to extrude the geometry outward from the body.

Still working out wing geometry...

Positioning each layer at offset x = s*(0.165+k), then shaping the base layer with a pink-to-coral gradient and starting on a coverts layer with a deeper coral scalloped outline defined by a set of u,v boundary points.

Still plotting feather coordinates...

Now I'm defining the coral polygon rows, upper and lower, with slight thickness and offset so their layered faces stay just within the 7mm base boundary.

Adding small scapular tufts and keeping legs/neck plain, confirming the paint helpers (mottle, gradient, countershade) are exported and usable for body coloring. I'm sketching coordinate helper functions and planning the slab points for the wing webs.

Working out the hallux rod, toe chain, jaw joint, and beak sweep bone attachments...

Now I'm tuning the beak taper curves, giving the upper beak a thinning radius toward a black tip with a slight bulge at the bend, and mirroring that shape for the lower beak.

I'm positioning the eyes above the beak line using a local head-coordinate helper, placing them forward and outward with a pale yellow iris and black pupil, then starting the beak path geometry.

Now I'm assembling the neck bone with a smooth tapered radius sweep down to the head base, then adding the head as a scaled sphere positioned on that bone, double-checking whether the scale parameter accepts an array or needs a vector.

Since scale might only take a number, I'm switching to scaling the geometry itself directly using the sphere's built-in scale method, applying it similarly for the feather sticks with their own non-uniform proportions, and deciding to just create and reuse geometry instances rather than regenerating them for every call.

Now I'm setting up the feather colors, foot positioning based on left/right side, and sketching out the overall builder code structure for the flamingo, starting with hips and spine chains and a body sweep using catmull-rom curves.

Still writing skeleton code...

Setting limb bend direction consistently for all legs, sizing the water radius and position, and double-checking head height clears the water level before finalizing.
